title: Metrics Server & kubectl top 📊
description: Enable the core metrics pipeline and use kubectl top to check resource usage.

slides.title: The Resource Metrics Pipeline ⛓️
slides.content:
# Lightweight, built‑in metrics

The **Metrics Server** collects CPU and memory metrics from kubelets, stores them in memory, and serves them via the `metrics.k8s.io` API. It’s the standard source for:
- `kubectl top`
- Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA)
- `kubectl describe` resource usage

It does **not** persist data – it’s meant for short‑term, real‑time views.

slides.title: Installing Metrics Server 🛠️
slides.content:
## One command on most clusters

**minikube**:
```bash
minikube addons enable metrics-server
```
**kind / production**: apply the official YAML:
```bash
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server/releases/latest/download/components.yaml
```

Check it’s running:
```bash
kubectl get deployment metrics-server -n kube-system
```

slides.title: Verify Metrics API
slides.content: Check if the API is available:

quizData.question: Which component does the HPA use by default to get CPU/memory metrics?
quizData.explanation: Metrics Server provides the resource metrics API used by HPA and kubectl top.

slides.title: Using kubectl top 🖥️
slides.content:
## Real‑time resource usage

```bash
kubectl top nodes          # CPU & memory per node
kubectl top pods           # all Pods in current namespace
kubectl top pods -A        # all namespaces
kubectl top pod my-pod --containers  # per‑container
```

Output example:
```
NAME        CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
my-pod      45m          128Mi
```

Note: `m` = millicores (1000m = 1 core).

quizData.question: What does `kubectl top pods` show?

options.text: CPU and memory usage of Pods

quizData.explanation: It displays current CPU and memory consumption per Pod.

slides.title: Limitations of Metrics Server ⚠️
slides.content:
## Not for long‑term monitoring

- No historical data – only current snapshot.
- No custom metrics – only CPU and memory.
- No alerting or dashboards built‑in.

For production monitoring, you need Prometheus.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Metrics Server is a must‑have for HPA

Always install it, even if you use Prometheus for dashboards. HPA relies on it for resource‑based autoscaling out of the box.
